dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: sarvajñaḥ sarvakartā ca vyāpakaḥ parameśvaraḥ | sa evāhaṃ śaivadharmā iti dārḍhyāc chivo bhavet ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
sanskrit_variants: verse 109: GRETIL and Singh read śaivadharmā iti dārḍhyāc chivo bhavet; Pradīpaka applies sandhi (śaivadharmeti); Wallis and The Mystery Within read dārḍhyād bhavec chivaḥ. Meaning is the same.
dharana.rendering: 'The supreme Lord is all-knowing, all-doing and all-pervading. I am he, having the qualities of Śiva': through the firmness of this conviction, one becomes Śiva.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: the dhāraṇā of the first phase of recognition (pratyabhijñā): one is Śiva in essence, masked as an individual (jīva); when the individual intensely recognises its essential reality, the mask falls away and grace (anugraha) operates. Wallis: 'I have Śiva's qualities'.
dharana.technique_name: I Share the Qualities of Śiva
dharana.instruction: Recognise in yourself the qualities of the supreme: knowing, acting and pervading.

checked_against: The Mystery Within (2019), Session Two list: 'Dharana 85' = verse 109 (agrees with Singh)
Wallis concordance: verse 109 = 'I have Śiva’s qualities (Y84 ~ B3)' (verse text and technique match)
GRETIL, Wallis and Pradīpaka: Sanskrit of verse 109 compared
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: verse 109: I have Śiva’s qualities (Y84 ~ B3)
numbering_variants.mystery_within_parallel: The parallel-translations section of The Mystery Within labels verse 109 'Dharana 86', because from verse 106 on it gives every verse its own number (106 = 83 … 137 = 114). Singh and the same book's Session Two list put this at dhāraṇā 85. Not followed.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 109 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is recognition: the qualities of the whole found, in seed, in oneself.
geometry.svg_hint: a large circle and a small circle with the same pattern inside both
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Recognise it
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the sense of being a small, limited self gives way to recognising the qualities of the whole in oneself. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn attention toward what the verse names, and let everything else stay in the background
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The conviction 'I share the qualities of Śiva: knowing, doing, pervading'

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: 'The supreme Lord is all-knowing, all-doing and all-pervading. I am he, having the qualities of Śiva': through the firmness of this conviction, one becomes Śiva.
adiyogi.method_summary: Reflect on the qualities of the supreme: knowing everything, doing everything, present everywhere. Then recognise those same capacities in yourself: you know, you act, your awareness extends. Hold that recognition firmly and rest in it.

honesty.disclosure: Door 085 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 85 (verse 109) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 085 is dharana 85, verse 109. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
New door researched on 2026-10-06 on branch research/vbt-houses-2-7; awaiting guardian review.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. This is recognition of essential nature, not a claim to special powers. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Sit or lie down. The map is the whole's qualities found in oneself.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the floor or the chair carry you. Eyes closed or soft.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Knowing, doing, pervading: the supreme's qualities. You know, you act, your awareness extends. Recognise it. Hold it firmly.

beats.title: Reaction cue

beats.title: Adiyogi thread

beats.title: Exit / integrate
